c0868: HACCP Plan Template: Hazard Analysis & CCPs
c0870: It is the heart of the HACCP system: it identifies the hazards at each step of the process, decides which ones are critical control points and says, for each one, which limit must not be exceeded, who monitors it, what is done if it is exceeded, where it is recorded and who checks that all of this is being done.
c0871: ▸ It comes with 21 hazards analyzed across 7 steps: Receiving, Storage, Thawing, Preparation, Cooking, Holding & cooling, Service.

c0873: How the risk level is calculated
c0874: ▸ Likelihood and Severity are drop-downs (High / Medium / Low). The "Risk level" calculates itself: High=3, Medium=2, Low=1, and the product of the two gives Critical (9), High (6), Medium (3-4) or Low (1-2). It is color-coded.
c0875: ▸ The CCP decision follows a rule, not the judgment of the day: High or Critical risk with no later step that eliminates the hazard → CCP; High or Critical risk controlled by a prerequisite program (suppliers, cleaning, training) and with no limit that can be measured in real time → OPRP; Low or Medium risk → NO.
c0876: ▸ That is why allergen labeling at receiving and the allergen menu at service are listed as OPRP and not CCP: "complete label" and "up-to-date menu" are not measurable critical limits. The real allergen control is in the kitchen, and there it is a CCP.

c1159: PROTOCOL FOR A DECLARED ALLERGY — BEFORE COOKING AND AT SERVICE
c1160: Listen and WRITE the allergy on the order, naming the allergen. Never pass it on by word of mouth only.
c1161: Check the allergen matrix (template 08) for the COMPLETE dish: sauces, sides, breads, fried items and dressings included.
c1162: Tell the head chef before firing the order. ONE person prepares the dish, from start to finish.
c1163: Change your gloves, wash your hands and use a dedicated board, knife and utensils in a clear work area.
c1164: Do not share the fryer, oil, cooking water, griddle or toaster without cleaning them first: it is the most frequent route of cross-contact.
c1165: If you cannot guarantee the allergen is absent, SAY SO: "we cannot guarantee that this dish is free of …", and offer an alternative. Send the dish out separately, covered and labeled, and hand it over IN PERSON to the allergic guest.
c1166: IF A GUEST STARTS A REACTION
c1167: Call 911 (UK: 999) for any symptom: trouble breathing, swelling of the lips or tongue, dizziness, vomiting or widespread hives. You call for SYMPTOMS, not as a precaution. It is the FIRST thing you do.
c1168: If the person carries an epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it following their instructions —it is given at the same time as the call. Do not move them or leave them alone.
c1169: Stop serving immediately and keep the plate, the packaging and the product label: they will be needed to investigate what happened.
c1170: Log the incident the same day in template 11 (Corrective Action Log): dish, lot, who prepared it and what was done.
c1171: Print these charts and post them in the kitchen and at the bar. All staff, kitchen and front of house, must know the 14 allergens and this protocol.
